newsitem.title: USA: Perry to visit Bosnia on globe-circling trip.
newsitem.headline: Perry to visit Bosnia on globe-circling trip.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Perry will visit U.S. troops in Bosnia next week on a globe-circling trip that will also take him to the Gulf and Japan, the Pentagon announced on Friday.
Perry will begin his trip in Naples, Italy, next Wednesday and will spend Thursday -- the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday -- with American troops in Tuzla in Bosnia.
He will visit Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Qatar in the Gulf as well as Japan before returning to Washington on December 4.

Perry was expected to meet with Russian military officials in Bosnia to discuss participation by U.S. and Russian forces in a follow-on peacekeeping force in the former Yugoslav region next year. Both countries currently have troops serving in a NATO-led peace implementation force there.
Perry, 69, has announced he will resign after nearly three years as defence secretary as President Bill Clinton rebuilds his national security team after his November 5 re-election.
Speculation on his successor has centred around Central Intelligence Agency Director John Deutch, although other names are also mentioned.

In Saudi Arabia, Perry will hold talks with top Saudi officials on security in the region and was expected to visit an air base in the desert not far from Riyadh, to which most U.S. military personnel in the kingdom were recently moved.
The move was made following a bombing in Saudi Arabia last year and another in June of this year that killed a total of 24 American troops.
Perry said recently the United States had not identified the attackers, but published reports have said the Saudis have arrested about 40 persons in their own investigation.

After brief visits to Kuwait and Qatar, two moderate Gulf states where U.S. military equipment is pre-positioned for any future emergency in the region, Perry will go to Tokyo for talks on the status of American forces in Japan.

The United States agreed earlier this year to make some cuts in its military presence on the island of Okinawa following the rape of a Japanese school girl there by three U.S. military men. But Perry said the overall total of American troops stationed throughout Japan would not change.
